cues.zh: 我说我主要用 Windows 时，很多技术人都很惊讶。
cues.en: A lot of techies are surprised when I say I mostly use Windows.

cues.zh: 写代码、剪视频的人，为什么会用 Windows 呢？
cues.en: Why would anyone who writes code and edits video use Windows?

cues.zh: 两个原因：第一，更便宜。
cues.en: Two reasons: one, it's cheaper.

cues.zh: 第二：它能让我凑合拼凑。
cues.en: And two: it lets me bodge.

cues.zh: 所以坐稳了，没错，我会告诉你我是怎么做那个 emoji 键盘的，
cues.en: So sit back, 'cos, yes, I'll tell you how I made the emoji keyboard,

cues.zh: 但更重要的是，我要讲讲凑合拼凑的艺术。
cues.en: but more importantly, I will tell you about the art of the bodge.

cues.zh: Bodge 是个很妙的英式词，意思是拼凑起来、做临时修补。
cues.en: Bodging is a wonderful British word that means to patch together, to make temporary repairs.

cues.zh: 一个 bodge 很粗糙、不优雅、迟早会散架，但它能用。
cues.en: A bodge is clumsy, it's inelegant, it'll fall apart, but it'll work.

cues.zh: 而且只要有人在它坏掉时再凑合修一次，它就能一直用下去。
cues.en: And it'll keep working as long as there's someone around to bodge it again if it breaks.

cues.zh: 你还记得《阿波罗13号》里那段吗？他们得把方形的插头塞进圆孔里。
cues.en: You know that bit in Apollo 13 where they have to fit the square peg in the round hole?

cues.zh: 那就是个 bodge。实际上，那可能是人类历史上最伟大的 bodge。
cues.en: That is a bodge. Actually, that's possibly the greatest bodge in human history.

cues.zh: 其实，如果你能想到更好的，请在评论区告诉我，
cues.en: In fact, if you can think of a better one, let me know in the comments,

cues.zh: 因为历史上那些“神级凑合”大概都能写成一本书，
cues.en: 'cos there's probably a book on Great Bodges of History

cues.zh: 而我还挺想当那个写书的人。
cues.en: to be written there, and I'd quite like to be the one to write it.

cues.zh: 总之，凑合着做东西一直是我的风格。
cues.en: Anyway. Bodging has always sort of been how I make things.

cues.zh: 我没学过计算机科学，这里写的也不是什么优雅的解法，
cues.en: I didn't study computer science, I'm not writing elegant solutions here,

cues.zh: 我就是把东西拼凑起来。
cues.en: I patch things together.

cues.zh: 重要的事——备份、密码安全——我会确保做对……
cues.en: The important stuff-- backups, password security-- I make sure I get that right...

cues.zh: 但为了好玩做的东西，我就凑合。
cues.en: but stuff I'm making for fun, I bodge.

cues.zh: 几年前拍电视节目时，我才学会了正经地凑合。
cues.en: Now I learned to properly Bodge when I was filming a TV show a few years ago.

cues.zh: 那节目有些内容传到网上了，链接我会放在简介里，
cues.en: Some of that show's made it online, I'll put links in the description,

cues.zh: 不过先听我说，因为你需要了解一些背景。
cues.en: but stick with me for now, 'cos you need to know some context about it.

cues.zh: 我当时和两个人一起拍摄。Colin Furze，你可能在YouTube上见过他，他做那些荒唐的、
cues.en: I was filming with two people. Colin Furze, who you might know off YouTube, he makes ludicrous,

cues.zh: 巨大的、会爆炸的实体玩意儿，还保持着电动代步车的陆地速度纪录。
cues.en: big, exploding physical things, and he has the land speed record for a mobility scooter.

cues.zh: 然后是 Charles Yarnold，他用 Arduino 和电路板制作
cues.en: And then there was Charles Yarnold, who makes

cues.zh: 精巧的微电子装置。
cues.en: intricate microelectronics with Arduinos and circuit boards.

cues.zh: 比如去年，Charles 做了 Barack Obama 的圣诞树。
cues.en: Like, last year Charles made Barack Obama's Christmas tree.

cues.zh: 人们可以在线定制颜色和图案，
cues.en: And people could go online to customise the colours and patterns

cues.zh: 控制树上上下下闪烁的彩灯。太棒了。
cues.en: of the twinkly lights that went up and down it. It was wonderful.

cues.zh: 我在那个电视节目里的工作，就是做这两者之间的桥梁，连接 Colin 和 Charles，
cues.en: And my job on the TV show was to be the bridge between those two, between Colin and Charles,

cues.zh: 让他们亲手制作出来的作品
cues.en: to get the creations that they physically fabricated

cues.zh: 能与外界、也能彼此协同运作。
cues.en: working with the world and with each other.

cues.en: So when we made a remote control for a horse --

cues.zh: 没开玩笑，我们真的给一匹马做了遥控器——
cues.en: I'm not kidding, we made a remote control for a horse --

cues.zh: Colin 搭建了机器人骑手的框架，
cues.en: Colin built the framework for a robot jockey,

cues.zh: Charles 做了所有电路和继电器，让它在收到信号时拉动缰绳，

cues.en: and I built a smartphone app that let you send those signals to let you steer a horse.

cues.zh: 而且成功了！
cues.en: And it worked!

cues.zh: 而且我大概是三个人里最轻松的，因为我做东西的时候，
cues.en: And I probably had the easiest job of the three of us, 'cos when I made things,

cues.zh: 我有撤销按钮。
cues.en: I had an undo button.

cues.zh: 但关键的是：我们在做原型。
cues.en: But the key part was this: we were building prototypes.

cues.zh: 它们只需要撑过一天的拍摄，我们会在现场。
cues.en: They had to work for one day of filming, and we'd be there for it.

cues.zh: 但它们必须在当天能用，否则电视节目会很糟糕
cues.en: But they HAD to work on that day, or the TV show would be terrible

cues.zh: 我们还会浪费一大笔钱。而我们基本没时间做。
cues.en: and we'd have wasted a lot of money. And we had basically no time to build there.

cues.zh: 我们每天工作16小时，一周7天，到制作结束时，
cues.en: We were working 16-hour days, 7-days a week, and by the end of production,

cues.zh: 我们没时间了。我们都在凑合拼凑。
cues.en: we had no time. We were bodging.

cues.zh: 而那个帮了我最多的软件，在那档节目和之后都是，
cues.en: And the bit of software that helped me, on that show and since, more than anything else,

cues.en: was called AutoHotKey.

cues.zh: AutoHotKey 是个太好用的拼凑工具，有时会被当成病毒检测出来。
cues.en: AutoHotKey is such a good bodging tool that it sometimes gets detected as a virus.

cues.zh: AutoHotKey 最初是想做得非常非常简单：
cues.en: AutoHotKey was originally meant to be really, really simple:

cues.zh: 它等待用户按下某个键，
cues.en: it waits until the user presses a certain key,

cues.zh: 然后启动一个程序，或者打出一些更长的文字，
cues.en: and then it starts a program, or it types some longer text,

cues.zh: 或者按下一串更复杂的按键命令，否则会非常难。
cues.en: or it presses a more complicated series of key commands that'd be really difficult otherwise.

cues.zh: 比如，你想让 F10 键让你的游戏角色突然转身 180 度并开火？
cues.en: Like, if you wanted your F10 key to make your video game character suddenly spin 180 and fire?

cues.zh: 明白了。没问题。是 AutoHotKey 吧。
cues.en: Got it. No problem. AutoHotKey was it.

cues.zh: 问题是，AutoHotKey 不断壮大、壮大、再壮大。
cues.en: The thing is, AutoHotKey grew and grew and grew and grew.

cues.zh: 而它的脚本语言，也就是你为了让它工作而必须编写的东西，
cues.en: And its scripting language, the stuff you have to write in to make it work,

cues.zh: 糟透了。我是说真的非常糟糕。
cues.en: is terrible. I mean really awful.

cues.zh: 它本来只打算做非常简单的事情，
cues.en: It was meant to do just really simple things,

cues.zh: 但随着时间的推移，它获得了做很多事情的能力。
cues.en: and over time it's gained the ability to do so much.

cues.zh: 它能读取文件，能查看屏幕上单个像素的颜色，
cues.en: It can read files, it can look at the colour of individual pixels on screen,

cues.zh: 它能调用任意的 Windows DLL，
cues.en: it can call arbitrary Windows DLLs,

cues.zh: 它能解析正则表达式，给那些知道那是什么的人。
cues.en: it can parse regular expressions, for anyone who knows what those are.

cues.zh: 但这一切都是用这种奇怪的、非标准的方式实现的，灵感来自 Visual Basic。
cues.en: But it's all in this weird non-standard way that is inspired by Visual Basic.

cues.zh: AutoHotKey 是一个拼凑之物，帮你制作其他拼凑之物。
cues.en: AutoHotKey is a bodge that helps you make other bodges.

cues.zh: 但它确实能用！
cues.en: But it works!

cues.zh: 这意味着你不必花上好几个小时
cues.en: And it means that instead of having to spend hours of time

cues.zh: 钻研复杂的操作系统层面的东西，
cues.en: diving into complicated operating-system-level stuff,

cues.zh: 只要写几行脚本，就能搞定。
cues.en: you just write a few lines of script and it does the job.

cues.zh: 在那档电视节目里，我用 AutoHotKey 控制了一名跳伞者降落伞的释放。
cues.en: I used AutoHotKey, on the TV show, to control the release of a skydiver's parachute.

cues.zh: 而且成功了。我是说，效果非常好。我们确实有备用方案，但它真的成功了。
cues.en: And it worked. I mean, really well. I mean, we had a reserve, but it worked.

cues.zh: 我为那档节目搞过的最牛的临时拼凑方案，我发誓这是真的，
cues.en: The greatest bodge I ever pulled for that TV show involved, and I swear this is true,

cues.zh: 用了一台 Mac 上的语音合成器和一个 Sibelius 副本，
cues.en: a voice synthesiser and a copy of Sibelius on a Mac

cues.zh: 由一台 Windows PC 上的 AutoHotKey 远程控制，
cues.en: being remote-controlled by AutoHotKey on a Windows PC,

cues.zh: 那台 PC 在盲目地拖动鼠标，
cues.en: which was blindly dragging the mouse around

cues.zh: 通过远程桌面连接执行预先录制的动作，
cues.en: doing pre-recorded movements through a remote desktop connection,

cues.zh: 同时另一台 PC 通过 Wi-fi 向 Mac 上打开的 Google Chrome 窗口发送命令，
cues.en: while another PC fired commands to a Google Chrome window open on the Mac over Wi-fi,

cues.zh: 因为 AppleScript 以及我们想在 Sibelius 上运行的所有类似 Mac 工具
cues.en: because AppleScript and all the similar tools for Mac that we needed to run on Sibelius

cues.zh: 根本应付不了这么离谱的事。
cues.en: just weren't up to doing something that ridiculous.

cues.zh: 顺便说一句，要是有人建议用 Linux……不行。
cues.en: By the way, if anyone out there suggests using Linux... no.

cues.zh: 全世界都爱 emoji。
cues.en: The world loves emoji.

cues.zh: 我是说，认真的。个别人可能不爱，当然。
cues.en: I mean, seriously. Individual people might not, sure.

cues.zh: 我自己其实不怎么用，尽管键盘上有，
cues.en: I don't really use them myself, despite the keyboard,

cues.zh: 但全世界都爱它们。人们会点开关于 emoji 的标题。
cues.en: but the world loves them. People click on headlines about emoji.

cues.zh: 只要标题里带上这个词，点击量就会高得多得多。
cues.en: Just putting the word in a headline means you get way, way more hits on it.

cues.en: Emoji is basically the Donald Trump of computers. There's a joke that won't date well.

cues.zh: 这名字本身就是标题党，你根本不需要再加别的东西。
cues.en: The very name is clickbait, you don't really need anything else on top of it.

cues.en: My friend Matt -- who's behind the camera right now -- say hi, Matt.

cues.en: Matt and I made an emoji-only messenger last year. And hardly anyone used it.

cues.zh: 还发邮件来跟我们谈股权。
cues.en: and emailing us to talk about equity.

cues.zh: 所以今年，电影公司在竞标一个基于emoji的创意方案。
cues.en: So this year, movie studios were bidding on an emoji-based pitch.

cues.zh: 可惜不是我的。我真希望是我想出来的，
cues.en: Not mine, sadly. I wish I'd thought of it,

cues.zh: 因为他们靠这个拿到了近一百万美元。
cues.en: because they got nearly a million dollars for it.

cues.zh: 全世界都爱emoji。
cues.en: The world loves emoji.

cues.zh: 而关键在于：我们今天所熟知的emoji概念，
cues.en: And here's the thing: the concept of emoji, as we know it today,

cues.zh: 也就是这个键盘上的这些，其实是个拼凑的产物。
cues.en: as is on this keyboard, is a bodge.

cues.zh: 你可能知道这个故事。
cues.en: You know, you might know the story.

cues.zh: 在世界各地，每种语言都有不同的方式
cues.en: Around the world, every language had a different way of translating

cues.zh: 在字母和二进制代码（1和0）之间为计算机做转换。
cues.en: between letters and binary code, 1s and 0s, for computers.

cues.zh: 当时日本的文字编码方案里还有点空间，
cues.en: Now Japan had a bit of space in its text encoding scheme,

cues.zh: 毕竟他们的字符本来就比拉丁字母多得多，
cues.en: they've got a lot more characters than the Latin alphabet anyway,

cues.zh: 所以再加几个字符根本不成问题。
cues.en: so adding a few more wouldn't really have been a problem.

cues.zh: 有位聪明的工程师想：“等等，
cues.en: And some clever engineer thinks, "Hang on,

cues.zh: “我们可以在文本编码里放小图片，让人们发送这些，
cues.en: "we can put little pictures in our text encoding, we can let people send those,

cues.zh: “这样就能发送图片，而无需真的传输图片
cues.en: "and we can send pictures without actually having to send pictures

cues.zh: 以及随之而来的全部带宽。”
cues.en: with all the bandwidth that entails."

cues.zh: 所以有几个相互竞争的版本，
cues.en: So there are a few competing versions of that,

cues.zh: 但它们一直没离开日本，直到Unicode联盟出现。
cues.en: but they never left Japan until the Unicode Consortium came along.

cues.zh: Unicode联盟的工作是前往每个国家
cues.en: Now, the Unicode Consortium's job is to go to every country

cues.zh: 弄清他们如何将文本编码成二进制，
cues.en: to work out how they encode text into binary,

cues.zh: 并把所有这些数百种相互竞争的方法整合成一个全球大标准。
cues.en: and turn all of these hundreds of competing approaches into one big worldwide standard.

cues.zh: 最令人惊叹的是，在很大程度上，
cues.en: The most amazing thing about it is that for the most part,

cues.zh: 他们确实成功做到了。
cues.en: they actually managed to make that work.

cues.zh: 但Unicode本应是双向的。
cues.en: But Unicode was meant to be two-way.

cues.zh: 你把文本转换成Unicode，然后再转换回
cues.en: You convert text into Unicode, then convert it back out

cues.zh: 你国家的旧有遗留系统，不应有任何丢失。
cues.en: into your country's old legacy system, and nothing should be lost.

cues.zh: 于是 Unicode 团队到了日本，他们说：“哦，你们……
cues.en: So the Unicode team get to Japan and they go, "Oh, you've...

cues.zh: “你们在文本里放了图片。好吧，嗯……
cues.en: "You've put pictures in your text. Okay, um...

cues.zh: “我们能处理。我们会把它们作为小字形加进标准里。
cues.en: "We can deal with that. We'll add them to the standard as little glyphs.

cues.zh: 没问题。我们本来就有个笑脸符号。没人会注意的。”
cues.en: That's fine. We had a smiley face in there anyway. No-one'll notice."

cues.zh: 确实有一阵子没人注意，直到苹果想在日本卖 iPhone，
cues.en: And no-one does notice, really, for a while, until Apple, who want to sell iPhones in Japan,

cues.zh: 悄悄把 emoji 加成了一个……相当隐蔽的选项。
cues.en: quietly add emoji as a... a fairly hidden option.

cues.en: so they make it so you can use something called a zero-width joiner to

So: fifth key. 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.

cues.zh: 它会判断你想要哪个数字表情，并把那个数字保存到磁盘上的文件里。

cues.zh: 然后，它按下 F24 键。没错，确实有 F24 键。

cues.zh: 但出于向后兼容性，Windows 仍然能处理这个键。
cues.en: but it's still a key that Windows can deal with because backwards compatibility.

cues.zh: AutoHotKey 在监听那个 F24 键，当它听到时，
